newsitem.title: USA: Best Products sells assets; cuts another 5,500 jobs.
newsitem.headline: Best Products sells assets; cuts another 5,500 jobs.

text.p: Best Products Co. Inc., the retailer that created the catalogue showroom industry 40 years ago, says it is closing its doors for good and throwing its remaining 5,500 employees out of work.

The company, which has twice filed for bankruptcy protection, announced late Tuesday that it signed an agreement to sell most of its assets -- 88 stores and 11 jewellery-only units in 17 states -- to an investor group for $410 million.
"This is terrible news," said Frances Lewis, who along with her husband Sydney, founded Best in 1956. The couple no longer have any involvement in the chain.
Early this month, Best announced that it was shutting down some of its operations and holding liquidation sales at 81 stores in a move to cut 4,500 jobs.
Once it exits the retailing business, the chain will have laid off a total of 10,000 workers.
The Richmond, Va.-based company it expected to start having "going-out-of-business" sales at its remaining stores in late November.
About 3,500 full-time employees and 2,000 part-time employees will lose their jobs as a result of the sale of Best's assets, which is subject to approval by the U.S. Bankruptcy Court.

The closing will mark the end of a retailing era that began with a catalogue in 1956 and then a small store the following year. The business eventually grew into a $2 billion-plus chain. Last year, it had sales of $1.5 billion but lost $95.7 million.

In September, the company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, marking the second time it has sought protection in less than six years. It previously filed for bankruptcy in January 1991 and emerged in June 1994.
The last remaining large catalogue showroom retailer is Service Merchandise Co. Inc.
Daniel Levy, Best's chairman and chief executive officer, who was hired in April to save the chain, said it was the best alternative for the company and its creditors.
"This is a totally debilitating experience," he said in an interview. "This is not why I came here and what I wanted to have happen."
Levy said that business realities made the continued operation of Best stores impractical.

Officials of the investment group, which is comprised of Jubilee Limited Partnership III, Bernstein Financial Group LLC, Alco Capital Group Inc. and The Nassi Group LLC, had previously agreed to pay $395 million for its retail-assets.
Jubilee Limited is an affiliate of the Schottenstein family of Columbus, Ohio, owners of Value City Department Stores.
The proposed deal was filed late Tuesday with the bankruptcy court in Richmond, Va., and a hearing is scheduled for Nov. 19.
Best said it will seek court approval for severance and vacation pay benefits for eligible employees. The package could cost $19 million.
Once the assets are sold, Best essentially would be reduced to a corporate shell with more than $535 million in bankruptcy-related liabilities and cash from the proceeds of the asset sale.
